    StartersBodega Bay crab toastsCrab with mayo, lemon and chives piled on garlic rubbed sourdough toastsHow to make it250g crab meat2 tbsp mayonnaise1 lemon, juiced1 tbsp chopped chives1 pinch cayenne pepper8 small slices of sourdough1 garlic clove, cut in halfFold the crab with mayo, lemon juice, chives and cayenne.Toast the sourdough and rub with the cut garlic.Pile the crab on top and serve straight away.Lovebird goat cheese filo cupsCrisp filo cups filled with whipped goat's cheeseHow to make it4 sheets of filo pastry40g butter, melted120g goat's cheese, whipped100g frozen peas, blanched8 mint leavesCut the filo into squares and brush with melted butter.Press in layers into a mini muffin tin.Bake at 180°C for 8 minutes until crisp.Fill with whipped goat's cheese, peas and a mint leaf. Serve two to a plate.Cathy's birthday chicken salad sandwichesThe children's birthday party on the hillHow to make itAs written, serves 4Poached chicken folded with mayo, celery, toasted walnuts, grapes and tarragon, in soft white bread cut into party triangles.Poach 2 chicken breasts in simmering salted water for 15 minutes, cool and shred finely.Mix with 5 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 finely diced celery sticks, 40g chopped toasted walnuts, a handful of halved green grapes, 1 tbsp chopped tarragon, a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper.Butter 12 slices of soft white bread and fill 6 sandwiches.Trim the crusts and cut each into 4 triangles.Oysters on the half shellMrs Bundy says birds don't attack. Eat quickly.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsSan Francisco cioppinoSeafood stew of mussels, clams and fish in a tomato and white wine brothHow to make it1 brown onion, diced1 fennel bulb, sliced3 garlic cloves2 tbsp olive oil1 tin crushed tomatoes250ml white wine500ml fish stock500g mussels500g clams300g green prawns300g snapper fillets, cut into chunks1 sourdough loafSoften the onion, fennel and garlic in the oil.Add the tomatoes, wine and stock and simmer for 20 minutes.Add the mussels and clams, cover and cook until they open.Add the prawns and snapper and cook just until done. Serve with sourdough.Lydia's roast chicken with sage stuffingDinner at the Brenner farmhouseHow to make itAs written, serves 4Golden roast chicken filled with a sage, onion and bread stuffing, with roast potatoes, glazed carrots and a pan gravy made from the drippings.Heat the oven to 200°C.Soften 1 diced onion in 40g butter, then mix with 150g fresh breadcrumbs, chopped sage, 1 egg, salt and pepper.Stuff a 1.8kg chicken, rub with butter and salt and roast with 1kg halved potatoes tossed in oil for 1 hour 20 minutes.Glaze 500g sliced carrots in a pan with butter, 1 tbsp honey and a splash of water.Rest the chicken 15 minutes, stir 1 tbsp flour and 250ml stock into the tray for gravy.SweetsMeringue nests with lemon curdCrisp meringue nests filled with lemon curd and topped with speckled candy eggsHow to make it3 egg whites180g caster sugar1 jar lemon curd24 speckled chocolate eggsWhisk the egg whites and sugar over simmering water until hot, then beat to stiff peaks.Pipe small nests onto lined trays.Bake at 100°C for 90 minutes, then cool.Fill with lemon curd and top each with three speckled eggs.DrinksIrish coffeeHot coffee with Irish whiskey and brown sugar, topped with floating creamHow to make it60g ground coffee1 L water4 tsp brown sugar120ml Irish whiskey200ml thickened cream, lightly whippedBrew the coffee with the water.For each glass stir sugar into hot coffee with whiskey.Pour the cream over the back of a spoon so it floats.Rusty nailEnd of the world, says the drunk at the bar.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
